beats.say: Desmos is the graphing calculator built into the SAT. It draws anything you type that starts with y equals or x equals, and it gives each expression its own line.

card.text: Type y = ... to draw a graph

beats.say: When a question gives you an equation and asks about its graph, such as its intercepts or its highest point, type the equation in first and look before doing any algebra.

card.text: Graph first, then do the algebra

beats.say: In this video, we work through three examples, from an easy one to a hard one, and you will see every key press.
Easy example. Graph the line y equals two x plus one, and find the point where it crosses the y axis.
Open Desmos. The list of expressions is on the left, and the graph is on the right. We will type our equation into the first row.
Type y equals two x plus one. Desmos draws the line right away, with no extra buttons to press.
To read a point, click it. Grey dots mark important points like intercepts. Clicking the dot where the line meets the y axis shows the point zero comma one.
So the y-intercept is one. That matches the constant term in the equation, which is a good check on our work.
Medium example. Graph y equals x squared minus three, and find the lowest point of the curve.
We start with a fresh graph. An equation with x squared makes a curve called a parabola, which looks like a smile or a frown.
Type y equals x, then press the caret key and a two to make the exponent. Press the right arrow to leave the exponent, and type minus three. That arrow key is the step beginners miss most often.
The lowest point is the vertex. Click the bottom of the curve to see its grey dot, then click the dot. Desmos shows the point zero comma negative three.
The vertex has a y value of negative three, so the minimum value of this function is negative three.
Hard example. A function is y equals negative the quantity x minus three, squared, plus eleven. What is its maximum value, and where does it occur?
Real questions often hide the answer inside a longer equation. We will let Desmos do the heavy lifting, and skip the algebra completely.
Type the whole function exactly as written. Put parentheses around x minus three, add the squared with the caret key, and press the right arrow before typing plus eleven.
Click the top of the curve, then click its grey dot. The maximum occurs at x equals three, where y equals eleven.
So the maximum value is eleven, and it occurs when x is three. If a graph ever disappears, zoom out with the minus button, because it is usually just off the screen.
To recap. Type the equation in first, and look at the graph before you start any algebra.
Click a curve, then click a grey dot, to read intercepts, vertices, and intersections exactly.
beats.item: Click grey dots to read points

beats.say: If the graph seems to vanish, zoom out, because it is usually just off the screen. In the next video, we find where graphs cross.
beats.item: Zoom out if the graph vanishes
